Tomato___Late_blight.Symptoms: Large water-soaked dark green-black lesions on leaves and stems with white mold.
Tomato___Late_blight.Cause: Phytophthora infestans oomycete pathogen thriving in cool, wet, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.Biological Treatment: Pre-treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) soil drenching.
Tomato___Late_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g/L.
Tomato___Late_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L.
Tomato___Late_blight.Prevention Tips: Ensure high-ridge planting for efficient drainage.
Tomato___Late_blight.Immediate Precautions: Isolate affected field patch; avoid morning harvesting.
Tomato___Late_blight.Future Prevention: Use certified late-blight resistant tomato cultivars.
Tomato___Late_blight.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface with velvety olive-green fungal mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Cause: Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) fungus thriving in high humidity (>85%) and poor ventilation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5mL/L.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Organic Recommendation: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or liquid sulfur spray.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Prevention Tips: Increase greenhouse ventilation and lower indoor relative humidity below 85%.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Immediate Precautions: Prune overcrowded lower branches to promote air movement.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Future Prevention: Select leaf mold resistant tomato varieties (Cf-9 gene).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Recovery Advice: Fungal velvety growth dries up in 7-10 days.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and greyish centers containing tiny black dots.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Cause: Septoria lycopersici fungus spread by rain splash and field tools.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Chemical Treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Organic Recommendation: Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Neem seed kernel extract (5%).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Prevention Tips: Mulch heavy around tomato roots and use drip irrigation.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Immediate Precautions: Remove lower infected leaves before spots reach upper canopy.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Future Prevention: Rotate away from tomatoes, potatoes, and eggplant for 2 years.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Recovery Advice: Septoria spot expansion halts in 7 days.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Symptoms: Fine yellow speckling/bronzing on upper leaves with delicate silk webbing underneath.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Cause: Tetranychus urticae mites multiplying rapidly in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Biological Treatment: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) or Chrysoperla carnea.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Chemical Treatment: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1mL/L or Abamectin 1.9% EC @ 0.5mL/L.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 3% + insecticidal potassium soap (5mL/L) on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Prevention Tips: Keep field perimeters wet and dust-free to discourage spider mite buildup.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Immediate Precautions: Direct spray nozzles thoroughly at undersides of leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Future Prevention: Avoid over-application of synthetic pyrethroid insecticides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Recovery Advice: New leaf growth emerges un-speckled within 5-7 days.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Target_Spot.Symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots expanding into brown lesions with faint concentric rings.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Cause: Corynespora cassiicola fungus favored by warm temperatures (20-30°C) and long dew periods.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1mL/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1g/L.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Organic Recommendation: Spray Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L combined with neem oil.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Prevention Tips: Avoid planting near older infected solanaceous crop fields.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Immediate Precautions: Improve plant staking and row aeration.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Future Prevention: Perform field sanitation and turn under crop debris post-harvest.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Recovery Advice: Target spots dry up and stop expanding within 7 days.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Symptoms: Severe upward leaf curling, yellowing leaf margins, stunted plant growth, and flower drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) transmitted exclusively by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Biological Treatment: Set up yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) to catch whiteflies; spray Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5g/L.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Chemical Treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5mL/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L to eliminate whitefly vectors.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 5% or pongamia oil (5mL/L) every 5 days.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Prevention Tips: Use 40-mesh insect-proof netting over nurseries and young seedling beds.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Immediate Precautions: Rogue out severely stunted virused plants early to reduce vector inoculum.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Future Prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., Ty-1/Ty-3 gene cultivars).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Recovery Advice: Vector control stops virus spread to healthy neighboring plants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, and fern-like leaves.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Cause: Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV) mechanically transmitted via hands, tools, and clothing.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Biological Treatment: Soak seeds in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) solution for 30 mins before sowing.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Chemical Treatment: No chemical cure for virus; focus on hygiene and tool sterilization.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray with skimmed milk (10%) to neutralize viral particle transfer.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Prevention Tips: Wash hands with soap and water before handling tomato plants; do not smoke near plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Immediate Precautions: Sanitize pruning shears with 70% alcohol or 10% bleach solution between rows.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

Tomato___healthy.Symptoms: No spots or lesions. Stems and foliage are vibrant green and structurally strong.
Tomato___healthy.Cause: Optimal soil moisture, balanced nutrition, and clean field hygiene.
Tomato___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens as bio-protectants once every 14 days.
Tomato___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Spray neem oil 3% or vermicompost wash to maintain foliar immunity.
Tomato___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain 60cm row spacing for adequate sunlight penetration and airflow.
Tomato___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Avoid flood irrigation during high-humidity evenings.
Tomato___healthy.Future Prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Tomato___healthy.Recovery Advice: Field is in optimal health. Continue standard fertigation.
Tomato___healthy.Cultural Management: Maintain optimal row spacing and field hygiene.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.Symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped lesions with grayish centers and reddish-brown borders on leaf blades.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Cause: Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia oryzae) fungus encouraged by high nitrogen levels and leaf wetness.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L during early morning.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Chemical Treatment: Apply Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5mL/L water.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Organic Recommendation: Spray Panchagavya 3% or Vermiwash 10% solution combined with Neem oil (3%).
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Prevention Tips: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertigation; split nitrogen into 3-4 applications.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Immediate Precautions: Drain standing water from field for 2-3 days to reduce canopy humidity.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Future Prevention: Cultivate blast-resistant varieties like ADT 43, CO 51, or CR Dhan 305.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Recovery Advice: Visible suppression of diamond spots expected within 8-10 days.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Rice___Bacterial_blight.Symptoms: Wavy yellow-to-brown wilting stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, progressing downwards.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Cause: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacteria entering leaf hydathodes and root wounds.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Biological Treatment: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed + foliar spray @ 1kg/ha.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L water.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Fresh cow dung slurry supernatant (5%) or turmeric powder extract.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Prevention Tips: Drain excess field water and avoid clipping leaf tips during transplanting.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Immediate Precautions: Refrain from excessive top-dressing of urea fertilizer.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Future Prevention: Grow resistant rice varieties such as Improved Samba Mahsuri (RP Bio-226).
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Recovery Advice: Bacterial spread halts within 5-7 days following copper-streptomycin application.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

Rice___Brown_spot.Symptoms: Oval or circular dark brown spots with yellow halos evenly distributed across mature leaf blades.
Rice___Brown_spot.Cause: Bipolaris oryzae fungus associated with nutrient-deficient (potassium & zinc) or drought-stressed soils.
Rice___Brown_spot.Biological Treatment: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5kg/ha mixed with 100kg farmyard manure.
Rice___Brown_spot.Chemical Treatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L.
Rice___Brown_spot.Organic Recommendation: Foliar application of wood ash slurry (5%) and zinc sulfate (0.5%).
Rice___Brown_spot.Prevention Tips: Maintain balanced soil fertility, applying Zinc Sulfate @ 25kg/ha at basal planting.
Rice___Brown_spot.Immediate Precautions: Provide timely irrigation to relieve moisture stress.
Rice___Brown_spot.Future Prevention: Conduct soil test and replenish potassium and organic matter prior to next season.
Rice___Brown_spot.Recovery Advice: Leaf vigor recovers in 10 days upon nutrient replenishment and spray.
Rice___Brown_spot.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins that rapidly turn yellow to white, wilting young seedlings (kresek).
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Cause: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacteria spread through rain, wind, and irrigation water.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Immediate Precautions: Drain excess standing water from the field and avoid high nitrogen top-dressing.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Prevention Tips: Use resistant rice varieties, maintain balanced soil nutrition, and burn infected crop stubble.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Organic Recommendation: Spray Fresh Neem Kernel Extract 5% or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Chemical Treatment: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L combined with Copper Oxychloride 3g/L.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Recovery Advice: Lesion expansion slows down and new tillers show healthy green foliage within 10-12 days.

Rice___Leaf_smut.symptoms: Small, slightly raised black linear spots scattered on leaf blades that rupture to release dark spores.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Cause: Entyloma oryzae fungus favored by high nitrogen fertilization and damp weather.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Immediate Precautions: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization and avoid flooding rice paddies.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Prevention Tips: Rotate crops seasonally, balance N-P-K fertilizer applications, and remove field weeds.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/L or neem oil 3% solution.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Chemical Treatment: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Recovery Advice: Infection stabilizes and fresh leaves emerge clean within 7-10 days.

Tomato___Early_Blight.Symptoms: Dark brown concentric target-like rings on mature lower leaves with yellow halos.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Cause: Alternaria solani fungal spores spread via wind, splashing rain, and residues.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis (2g/L) or Trichoderma harzianum (5g/L).
Tomato___Early_Blight.Chemical Treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply copper oxychloride (3g/L) mixed with 1% milk solution or neem oil.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Prevention Tips: Mulch soil around base with straw to stop soil splash.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Immediate Precautions: Prune and burn infected bottom leaves immediately.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Future Prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and maintain strict Solanaceae crop rotation.
Tomato___Early_Blight.Cultural Management: Ensure proper field sanitation, remove infected plant debris, and practice crop rotation.

Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Symptoms: Clusters of small green/black aphids on tassels, whorls, and leaf undersides secreting sticky honeydew followed by sooty mold.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Cause: Rhopalosiphum maidis (Corn leaf aphid) feeding on plant sap during dry, warm weather.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Biological Treatment: Release Chrysoperla carnea (Green lacewings) @ 50,000/ha or spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Chemical Treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5mL/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L water.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Organic Recommendation: Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or potassium salt of fatty acids (insecticidal soap @ 5mL/L).
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Prevention Tips: Conserve natural predators like coccinellid ladybird beetles and avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Immediate Precautions: Spray clear water or soap solution on heavily colonized tassels.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Future Prevention: Intercrop maize with cowpea or pulses to enhance beneficial predator populations.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Recovery Advice: Infestation controlled within 3-5 days of systemic insecticide or biopesticide spray.
Corn_(maize)___Aphid.Cultural Management: Practice timely sowing and eradicate weed hosts like Johnson grass around field borders.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Symptoms: Small, circular to oval chlorotic spots with brown centers and distinct yellowish halos on maize leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Cause: Curvularia lunata fungus favored by warm (28-32°C) humid weather with frequent rainfall.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Biological Treatment: Apply Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/L or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L foliar spray.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L at first symptom appearance.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of 20% cow urine solution or copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Prevention Tips: Collect and destroy post-harvest maize stover and practice 2-year crop rotation.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Immediate Precautions: Avoid sprinkler irrigation during late evenings.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Future Prevention: Sow certified disease-free seeds treated with Thiram @ 3g/kg seed.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Recovery Advice: New foliage emerges clean within 7-10 days following fungicide application.
Corn_(maize)___Curvularia_leaf_spot.Cultural Management: Ensure balanced NPK fertilization (120:60:40 kg/ha) with adequate potash.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Symptoms: Ragged shot-hole perforations on leaves, heavy window-pane feeding, and coarse sawdust-like frass accumulated in the whorl.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Cause: Spodoptera frugiperda (Fall Armyworm) larval feeding on leaf whorls and young tassels.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Biological Treatment: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) kurstaki @ 2g/L or Metarhizium anisopliae @ 5g/L in central whorl.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4mL/L or Emamectin benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L directed into the whorl.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Organic Recommendation: Whorl application of dry sand + lime (9:1 ratio) or 5% Neem cake powder.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Prevention Tips: Install FAW pheromone traps @ 12 traps/ha for early adult monitoring.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Immediate Precautions: Handpick and destroy egg masses and early-instar larvae in smallholder plots.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Future Prevention: Adopt push-pull technology by intercropping with Desmodium and planting Napier grass on borders.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Recovery Advice: Whorl feeding halts within 48-72 hours of targeted spray; fresh heart leaves emerge healthy.
Corn_(maize)___FAW_symptoms.Cultural Management: Synchronize community sowing and avoid staggered plantings across neighboring plots.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Symptoms: Visible caterpillars with inverted Y mark on head and 4 square dots on 8th abdominal segment feeding inside the central whorl.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Cause: Spodoptera frugiperda larvae destructive to all maize growth stages.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Biological Treatment: Release egg parasitoids Trichogramma pretiosum @ 50,000/ha or spray Spodoptera frugiperda NPV (SfNPV) @ 2mL/L.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Chemical Treatment: Apply Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5mL/L or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.3mL/L targeted into whorls.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Organic Recommendation: Spray Azadirachtin 10000 ppm @ 1.5mL/L or Bacillus thuringiensis var. aizawai @ 2g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Prevention Tips: Set up solar light traps @ 1/acre to trap and kill night-flying adult moths.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Immediate Precautions: Direct knapsack spray nozzle directly into the central funnel/whorl of each plant.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Future Prevention: Apply seed treatment with Cyantraniliprole 19.8% + Thiamethoxam 19.8% FS @ 6mL/kg seed.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Recovery Advice: Larval mortality achieved within 24-48 hours; crop vigor rebounds in 7 days.
Corn_(maize)___Fall_armyworm.Cultural Management: Maintain deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to predatory birds and solar heat.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Symptoms: Small diamond-shaped or rectangular lesions (1-3 cm) with buff centers and reddish-brown borders between leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Cause: Bipolaris maydis (Helminthosporium maydis) fungal pathogen favored by warm (25-30°C) damp conditions.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L or Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1mL/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Organic Recommendation: Foliar application of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L combined with 2% neem oil.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Prevention Tips: Bury crop residue deeply through moldboard ploughing after harvest.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Immediate Precautions: Strip lower severely infected leaves to reduce secondary spore dispersal.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Future Prevention: Cultivate resistant maize hybrids like Bio 9681, PAC 740, or HQPM 1.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Recovery Advice: Lesion expansion ceases within 6-8 days after systemic fungicide application.
Corn_(maize)___Maydis_leaf_blight.Cultural Management: Maintain balanced plant nutrition and avoid excessive plant density.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Symptoms: Vivid chlorotic yellow striping on leaves, stunted growth, downy white fungal growth on leaf undersides, and crazy top tassel deformation.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Cause: Peronosclerospora sorghi oomycete pathogen spread by soil-borne oospores and airborne conidia.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Biological Treatment: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed + foliar spray @ 5g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Chemical Treatment: Spray Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of Bio-sulfur @ 3g/L or Fermented Panchagavya 3% spray.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Prevention Tips: Avoid planting maize immediately after sorghum in endemic regions.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Immediate Precautions: Rogue out and burn all systemically infected stunted plants immediately to halt conidial spread.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Future Prevention: Treat seeds with Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 4g/kg seed prior to planting.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Recovery Advice: Non-systemic secondary infections subside within 7 days; rogue systemic cases.
Corn_(maize)___Sorghum_downy_mildew.Cultural Management: Ensure good drainage and sow early with the onset of monsoon.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Maize___healthy.Symptoms: Leaves are uniformly vibrant green, upright, free of spots, frass, or discoloration, showing strong vigorous vegetative growth.
Maize___healthy.Cause: None. Optimal agronomic health and balanced nutrient uptake.
Maize___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply VAM (Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza) or Azospirillum biofertilizers for root health.
Maize___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of 3% Panchagavya or seaweed extract @ 2mL/L for enhanced photosynthetic vigor.
Maize___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain scheduled irrigation at knee-high, tasseling, and silking stages.
Maize___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Monitor field weekly for early pest sightings like Fall Armyworm.
Maize___healthy.Future Prevention: Continue recommended NPK schedule (120:60:40 kg/ha) with zinc sulfate @ 25 kg/ha.
Maize___healthy.Recovery Advice: Crop is completely healthy. Continue standard agronomic practices.
Maize___healthy.Cultural Management: Maintain clean field bunds, weed-free status, and proper earthing up at 30-35 DAS.

source.organization: ICAR - Indian Council of Agricultural Research & CIBRC

Rice___False_smut.Symptoms: Individual rice grains in the panicle transform into large velvety yellowish-green or orange-green spore balls (smut balls).
Rice___False_smut.Cause: Ustilaginoidea virens fungus favored by high relative humidity (>90%) and cloudy, drizzly weather during flowering.
Rice___False_smut.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L during boot leaf stage.
Rice___False_smut.Chemical Treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L or Trifloxystrobin 25% + Tebuconazole 50% WG @ 0.4g/L at boot-leaf emergence.
Rice___False_smut.Organic Recommendation: Foliar application of Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or 5% Panchagavya spray.
Rice___False_smut.Prevention Tips: Avoid heavy nitrogen application, especially during panicle initiation and flowering stages.
Rice___False_smut.Immediate Precautions: Collect and discard smutted panicles in polybags before threshing to prevent soil contamination.
Rice___False_smut.Future Prevention: Perform seed treatment with Thiram 75% WP @ 3g/kg seed and hot water treatment at 52°C for 10 min.
Rice___False_smut.Recovery Advice: Preventive sprays at boot leaf stage protect uninfected panicles completely.
Rice___False_smut.Cultural Management: Maintain moderate plant spacing and manage field bund weeds.

Rice___Leaf_folder.Symptoms: Leaves folded longitudinally with white transparent longitudinal streaks where caterpillars have scraped green chlorophyll.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Cause: Cnaphalocrocis medinalis (Rice leaf folder) larvae spinning silk to roll leaf blades.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Biological Treatment: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 100,000/ha or spray Bacillus thuringiensis @ 2g/L.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3mL/L or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.25mL/L.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Organic Recommendation: Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Azadirachtin 10000 ppm @ 2mL/L.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Prevention Tips: Avoid shady over-fertilized field conditions and install light traps to attract adult moths.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Immediate Precautions: Pass a thorn branch or coir rope across the crop canopy to dislodge caterpillars before spraying.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Future Prevention: Avoid excessive use of pyrethroids that cause leaf folder resurgence.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Recovery Advice: Larvae eliminated in 48 hours; crop canopy regains green biomass in 7-10 days.
Rice___Leaf_folder.Cultural Management: Maintain wide border rows and practice alternate wetting and drying.

Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Symptoms: Oval to irregular greenish-gray water-soaked spots with dark brown margins on leaf sheaths near the waterline, spreading upward.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Cause: Rhizoctonia solani fungus thriving in high humidity, warm temperature (28-32°C), and dense canopies.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L or Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L at tillering.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2mL/L, Validamycin 3% L @ 2.5mL/L, or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1mL/L.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Organic Recommendation: Spray 10% cow dung slurry supernatant or fermented butter milk (5%) with neem oil.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Prevention Tips: Avoid high planting density (maintain 20x15 cm spacing) and split nitrogen doses.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Immediate Precautions: Drain field water for 48 hours and prune lower infected sheaths if practical.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Future Prevention: Treat nursery soil with Trichoderma-enriched compost @ 50 kg/ha.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Recovery Advice: Upward lesion progression ceases within 5-7 days after systemic triazole spray.
Rice___Leaf_sheath_blight.Cultural Management: Clean field bunds of weed hosts like Echinochloa colona.

Rice___Rice_skipper.Symptoms: Defoliated leaf margins with rolled leaf tubes containing stout green caterpillars with dark reddish-brown capsule heads.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Cause: Parnara mathias (Rice skipper) butterfly larvae feeding on leaf margins.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Biological Treatment: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma spp. @ 50,000/ha or spray Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorpyrifos 20% EC @ 2mL/L or Quinalphos 25% EC @ 2mL/L water.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Organic Recommendation: Spray 5% NSKE (Neem Seed Kernel Extract) with 0.5mL/L sticker.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Prevention Tips: Conserve natural spider and wasp parasitoid populations in the paddy ecosystem.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Immediate Precautions: Manually unroll leaf cases and destroy caterpillars in smallholder plots.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Future Prevention: Keep paddy bunds free of wild grass host plants.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Recovery Advice: Infestation controlled in 3-5 days; unaffected tillers compensate foliage rapidly.
Rice___Rice_skipper.Cultural Management: Practice synchronous planting in the contiguous farming zone.

Rice___White_stem_borer.Symptoms: Dead hearts (drying of central tiller shoot) in vegetative stage and white heads (empty, chaffy erect panicles) at reproductive stage.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Cause: Scirpophaga innotata (White stem borer) larvae boring into the base of the rice stem.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Biological Treatment: Release Trichogramma japonicum @ 100,000/ha weekly from 30 days after transplanting.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Chemical Treatment: Apply Cartap hydrochloride 4% G @ 18-20 kg/ha or spray Fipronil 5% SC @ 2mL/L.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Organic Recommendation: Install pheromone traps @ 20 traps/ha for mass trapping of male moths.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Prevention Tips: Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to remove egg masses.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Immediate Precautions: Maintain 5-7 cm standing water in field when applying granular insecticides.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Future Prevention: Plough stubbles immediately after harvest and submerge fields to kill overwintering larvae.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Recovery Advice: New tillers develop to compensate vegetative dead hearts within 10-14 days.
Rice___White_stem_borer.Cultural Management: Harvest crop close to ground level to reduce larval shelter in stubbles.

Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Symptoms: Central shoot drying (dead heart) during vegetative stage and completely white, unfilled erect panicles (white ears) during grain filling.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Cause: Scirpophaga incertulas (Yellow stem borer) monophagous pest boring into vascular cylinders of stems.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Biological Treatment: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma japonicum @ 100,000/ha 3 times at 10-day intervals.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Chemical Treatment: Apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% G @ 10 kg/ha or spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3mL/L.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Organic Recommendation: Apply 5% Neem cake in soil during transplanting and spray Azadirachtin 10000 ppm @ 2mL/L.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Prevention Tips: Set up Yellow stem borer sex pheromone traps (Scirpo-lure) @ 12 traps/ha.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Immediate Precautions: Clip seedling tip (top 2 cm) prior to transplanting to discard egg masses.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Future Prevention: Destroy post-harvest rice stubbles by deep tractor disc harrowing.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Recovery Advice: Dead heart damage arrested; compensatory tillering initiated within 7-10 days.
Rice___Yellow_stem_borer.Cultural Management: Avoid planting highly susceptible ultra-dense cultivars in endemic borer zones.

Rice___healthy.Symptoms: Lush green, erect foliage with healthy tillering, clean golden panicles, and no stem discoloration or leaf spotting.
Rice___healthy.Cause: None. Optimal agronomic health and balanced nutrient uptake.
Rice___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply Azospirillum and Phosphobacteria biofertilizers @ 2 kg/ha in root zone.
Rice___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Apply vermicompost @ 2 t/ha and spray 3% Panchagavya at panicle initiation.
Rice___healthy.Prevention Tips: Follow Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation protocol to save water and prevent root rot.
Rice___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Maintain routine scouting for early signs of leaf folder or stem borer.
Rice___healthy.Future Prevention: Ensure balanced NPK (120:40:40 kg/ha) with Zinc Sulfate @ 25 kg/ha basal application.
Rice___healthy.Recovery Advice: Crop is completely healthy. Continue standard agronomic practices.
Rice___healthy.Cultural Management: Keep field levees and irrigation channels clean and weed-free.

Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Symptoms: Water-soaked angular leaf spots bounded by leaf veins; black arm symptoms on stems and petioles; boll rot.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Cause: Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum bacteria favored by humid rainy weather.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Biological Treatment: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed + foliar spray of Neem oil (5mL/L).
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L + Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L water.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of Panchagavya 3% or NSKE 5% at 15-day intervals.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Prevention Tips: Use acid-delinted disease-free certified seeds. Rake and burn infected crop residues.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Immediate Precautions: Avoid sprinkler irrigation during active bacterial outbreak.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Future Prevention: Rotate cotton with sorghum or maize for 2 seasons.
Cotton___Bacterial_blight.Cultural Management: Maintain wide plant spacing for aeration and field drainage.

Cotton___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply bio-fertilizers Azospirillum and Phosphobacteria to maintain soil health.
Cotton___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Regular foliar spray of Vermicompost wash (10%).
Cotton___healthy.Prevention Tips: Monitor weekly for early sucking pest or bollworm infestation.

Sugarcane___Red_rot.Symptoms: Third or fourth leaf shows yellowing and drying at tips; internal stalk flesh shows red discoloration with white cross bands.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Cause: Colletotrichum falcatum fungus spread by infected setts and waterlogging.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Biological Treatment: Dip sugarcane setts in Trichoderma viride culture (10g/L) for 30 minutes before planting.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Chemical Treatment: Sett treatment with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 2g/L water before planting.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Organic Recommendation: Apply Neem cake @ 250kg/ha during final field preparation.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Immediate Precautions: Rogue out infected cane clumps and destroy immediately.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Future Prevention: Avoid continuous ratoon cropping in infected fields.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Recovery Advice: Rogue out affected clumps; manage healthy surrounding cane.
Sugarcane___Red_rot.Cultural Management: Ensure good drainage and avoid standing water.

Groundnut___Tikka_leaf_spot.Symptoms: Small circular dark brown spots on upper leaf surface with yellow halo (Early Leaf Spot) or dark black spots without halo (Late Leaf Spot).
Groundnut___Tikka_leaf_spot.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L or Trichoderma viride @ 5g/L.
Groundnut___Tikka_leaf_spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L water at first sign.
Groundnut___Tikka_leaf_spot.Organic Recommendation: Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at 14-day intervals.
Groundnut___Tikka_leaf_spot.Future Prevention: Rotate groundnut with cereal crops like pearl millet or sorghum.

Groundnut___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Ensure light irrigation at pod formation stage.

Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Symptoms: Concentric brown circular spots on leaves, stems, and pods; yellowing of leaf tissue.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Cause: Alternaria brassicae fungus favored by cool moist foggy winter weather.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/L or Garlic extract (5%).
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Chemical Treatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Iprodione 50% WP @ 2g/L water.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Organic Recommendation: Spray Cow urine (10%) + Neem oil (3mL/L) solution.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Prevention Tips: Sow mustard early (first fortnight of October) to escape disease onset.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Future Prevention: Use certified disease-resistant varieties like Pusa Mustard 26.
Mustard___Alternaria_blight.Cultural Management: Maintain optimum seed rate to avoid overcrowding.

Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Symptoms: Circular brown spots with dark concentric rings containing small black dots (pycnidia) on leaves and pods.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Cause: Ascochyta rabiei fungus favored by high humidity and cool temperatures.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Biological Treatment: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride (10g/kg seed) + foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L water.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply NSKE 5% spray at early vegetative stage.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Prevention Tips: Sow blight-resistant cultivars like C 235 or PBG 5.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Immediate Precautions: Avoid working in wet fields to prevent spore dissemination.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Future Prevention: Rotate chickpea with wheat or barley for 3 seasons.
Chickpea___Ascochyta_blight.Cultural Management: Destroy infected chickpea stubble after harvest.

Brinjal___Little_leaf.Symptoms: Extremely small light green crowded leaves giving a bushy rosette appearance; plant stays stunted and sterile.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Cause: Phytoplasma transmitted by leafhopper vector (Hishimonus phycitis).
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Neem oil (5mL/L) to control leafhopper vector + bio-pesticide Beauveria bassiana.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Chemical Treatment: Spray Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.7mL/L or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5mL/L water to control vectors.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Organic Recommendation: Spray 5% NSKE or Sticky Yellow Traps (10/acre) for leafhoppers.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Prevention Tips: Rogue out infected little leaf plants immediately and burn.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Immediate Precautions: Destroy alternative weed hosts around field borders.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Future Prevention: Grow nursery under insect-proof net mesh.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Recovery Advice: Vector control prevents further spread in field.
Brinjal___Little_leaf.Cultural Management: Keep field borders clean of solanaceous weeds.

Brinjal___healthy.Prevention Tips: Monitor for shoot and fruit borer.

Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Symptoms: Veins turn bright yellow creating a striking yellow network on green leaf; fruits become small, hard, and yellowish.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Cause: Bhendi Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus transmitted by whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Biological Treatment: Spray Verticillium lecanii @ 5g/L or Neem oil (5mL/L) for whitefly control.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Chemical Treatment: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L water to control whiteflies.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Organic Recommendation: Install Yellow Sticky Traps (15/acre) + Spray NSKE 5%.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Prevention Tips: Grow YVMC resistant okra varieties like Arka Anamika or Parbhani Kranti.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Immediate Precautions: Uproot infected yellow-veined plants and destroy.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Future Prevention: Sow border rows of maize or sorghum to trap whiteflies.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Recovery Advice: Whitefly suppression prevents field infection spread.
Okra___Yellow_vein_mosaic_virus.Cultural Management: Weed out wild malvaceous weed hosts.

Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Symptoms: Pale yellow streaks expanding into reddish-brown to black linear leaf spots with sunken gray centers.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Cause: Mycosphaerella fijiensis / musicola fungus favored by warm rainy weather.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis @ 5g/L or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L + mineral oil (1%).
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L water with sticker.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of Neem oil (5mL/L) mixed with soft soap solution.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Prevention Tips: Remove and burn severely spotted lower leaves.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Immediate Precautions: Improve plantation drainage and reduce sucker density.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Future Prevention: Maintain wide spacing (1.8m x 1.8m) for canopy airflow.
Banana___Sigatoka_leaf_spot.Cultural Management: Regular de-trashing of dead lower leaves.

Mango___Anthracnose.Symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions on young leaves, flowers, and fruits; causes blossom blight and fruit drop.
Mango___Anthracnose.Cause: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides fungus favored by wet weather during flowering and leaf flush.
Mango___Anthracnose.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L or Bacillus subtilis @ 5g/L.
Mango___Anthracnose.Chemical Treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 3g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L water during flush.
Mango___Anthracnose.Organic Recommendation: Spray Bordeaux mixture 1% or Liquid Copper Soap Fungicide (3mL/L).
Mango___Anthracnose.Prevention Tips: Prune criss-cross branches to open canopy to sunlight.
Mango___Anthracnose.Immediate Precautions: Remove dead twigs and infected panicles after harvest.
Mango___Anthracnose.Future Prevention: Spray protective copper fungicide before blossom opening.
Mango___Anthracnose.Cultural Management: Post-harvest hot water treatment of mango fruits at 52°C for 5 mins.
